raw_text:
name: dotnet-upgrade
description: .NET upgrade analysis and execution prompts.

Classify solution projects (`.NET Framework`, `.NET Core`, `.NET Standard`); inspect `.csproj` `TargetFramework` and SDK usage. Map internal/external dependency compatibility and graph depth; detect `packages.config` migrations to `PackageReference`. Order upgrades from least dependent libraries to APIs/Azure Functions. Plan incremental migration, rollback checkpoints, checklist, and **Upgrade Assistant** versus **manual upgrades**.

Select project targets (e.g., `net8.0`); update deprecated SDK/build settings, APIs, libraries, and `WebHostBuilder` → `HostBuilder` or `Startup.cs` → `Program.cs` patterns. Consider async conversion. Review NuGet, unsupported third-party, shared, legacy, and transitive dependencies; resolve conflicts and prefer Microsoft-supported alternatives.

Inspect YAML SDK pinning; update `UseDotNet@2` and `NuGetToolInstaller`. Provide .NET 8 pipeline snippets, feature-branch builds, CI build/test automation, and unit/integration validation. Verify runtime, logging, telemetry, connectivity, backward compatibility, API endpoints, and regressions. Plan UAT, production rollout, and post-deployment verification. Detect removed APIs using `.NET Upgrade Assistant` and API Analyzer; propose replacements.

Plan rollback-capable branches, partial/final commits, structured PRs (`Upgrade to .NET [Version]`), breaking-change tags, peer review, project-level change documentation, release notes, stakeholder communication, and progress dashboard/checklists. Recommend `.NET Upgrade Assistant`, `dotnet list package --outdated`, `dotnet migrate`, and `graph.json` dependency visualization. Generate dependency-analysis scripts, Copilot prompts, cross-repository validation workflows, final validation steps, build artifacts, test results, deployment checklist, and upgrade summary.
